name: package-license-viewer
description: Shows dependency license metadata inline in your project's manifest files.

commands.title: Package License Viewer: Refresh License Annotations
Package License Viewer: Clear License Cache
Package License Viewer: Toggle Inline License Annotations

packageLicenseViewer.format.markdownDescription: Template for the inline annotation. Placeholders: `${license}`, `${version}`, `${name}`, `${source}`, `${nodeEngine}`.

packageLicenseViewer.showResolvedVersion.description: Append the actually resolved version to the annotation (e.g. "MIT · 1.2.3").

packageLicenseViewer.showNodeEngine.markdownDescription: Append the package's declared `engines.node` range to the annotation, when it has one (e.g. `MIT (Node: >=20)`).

packageLicenseViewer.unknownText.description: Text shown when no license could be determined. Leave empty to show nothing.

packageLicenseViewer.annotationColor.markdownDescription: Theme color id used for the annotation (e.g. `editorCodeLens.foreground`, `descriptionForeground`), or a CSS color such as `#88888899`.

packageLicenseViewer.licenseColor.markdownDescription: Theme color id used for just the license part of the annotation (e.g. `charts.green`, `textLink.foreground`), or a CSS color such as `#4ec9b0`. Everything else keeps using `annotationColor`.

packageLicenseViewer.margin.description: CSS margin applied before the inline annotation.

packageLicenseViewer.cacheTtlHours.description: How long resolved licenses are cached, in hours. 0 disables persistent caching.

packageLicenseViewer.requestTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for a single registry request, in milliseconds.

packageLicenseViewer.maxConcurrentReques.description: Maximum number of registry requests performed in parallel.

packageLicenseViewer.npm.registry.description: Registry base URL used to look up packages that are not installed.

packageLicenseViewer.npm.useRegistry.description: Fall back to the registry when a package is not found in node_modules.

packageLicenseViewer.npm.useLockfiles.markdownDescription: Read `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock` or `bun.lock` to find the exact pinned version. This is what makes Yarn PnP and not-yet-installed workspaces work, and `package-lock.json` even carries the license itself.

packageLicenseViewer.npm.sections.description: Top-level package.json sections that are always annotated.

packageLicenseViewer.npm.autoDetectSecti.markdownDescription: Also annotate any other top-level object whose key ends with `dependencies` (e.g. `resolutions` style custom sections named `*Dependencies`).

packageLicenseViewer.npm.pnpmWorkspaceCa.markdownDescription: Also annotate the `catalog:` and `catalogs:` sections of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, where a workspace catalog's actual versions are declared.

packageLicenseViewer.jsr.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable annotations for Deno / import map manifests (`deno.json`, `deno.jsonc`, `jsr.json`, `import_map.json`).

packageLicenseViewer.jsr.registry.description: JSR registry base URL, used to resolve version ranges.

packageLicenseViewer.jsr.apiUrl.description: JSR API base URL, used to read the license of a resolved version.

packageLicenseViewer.crates.enabled.description: Enable license annotations for Cargo.toml dependency declarations.

packageLicenseViewer.crates.useRegistry.description: Allow crates.io requests. When disabled, existing cached public metadata may still be used.

packageLicenseViewer.crates.useLockfiles.description: Use a uniquely matching crates.io version from Cargo.lock before selecting a public version from the requirement.

packageLicenseViewer.moonbit.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable license annotations for MoonBit module manifests (`moon.mod`, `moon.mod.json`).

packageLicenseViewer.moonbit.useRegistry.description: Allow mooncakes.io requests. When disabled, installed modules, the local registry index and existing cached metadata are still used.

packageLicenseViewer.moonbit.useRegistry.markdownDescription: Read the registry index `moon update` keeps in `$MOON_HOME/registry/index`. It records every published version's license, so an installed toolchain resolves without any request.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm --prefix ../core run compile && npm run check-types && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.test:integration: npm run compile && npm run build-tests && vscode-test
